hook: The carbon in your body was, not long ago, carbon dioxide in the air. A plant pulled it in, you ate the plant, and you breathe some of it back out every few seconds. Other carbon has stayed locked in rock for a hundred million years. Burning coal, oil and natural gas takes that ancient carbon and puts it into the air in an instant.

ideas: Carbon moves between reservoirs (air, living things, soil, ocean, rock, fossil fuels); each movement is a flux.
Photosynthesis removes CO2; cellular respiration, decomposition and combustion release it.
A carbon sink takes in more carbon than it releases (forests, the ocean); a carbon source releases more than it takes in.
The fast cycle (air, life, ocean surface) turns over in days to centuries; the slow cycle (sedimentation, rock, fossil fuels) takes millions of years.

misconception.right: Trees take in CO2 but store the carbon, built into sugars, wood and leaves; the oxygen is released. Say "trees store carbon".

summary: Carbon cycles among the atmosphere, living things, soil, the ocean, sediments and rock, and fossil fuels. Photosynthesis removes CO2 from the air; respiration, decomposition and combustion return it. The ocean and growing forests act as carbon sinks. Burning fossil fuels moves slow-cycle carbon into the air far faster than sinks remove it, so atmospheric CO2 rises.
